chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Hamiri narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Which of the two was older, Ismail or Ishaq? And which of the two was the one to be sacrificed?

He said: Ismail was older than Ishaq by five years, and Ismail was the one to be sacrificed, and Makkah was the dwelling place of Ismail. And indeed, Ibrahim intended to sacrifice Ismail during the days of the season at Mina.
He said: And there were five years between Allah's glad tidings to Ibrahim regarding Ismail and His glad tidings regarding Ishaq,
Do you not hear the saying of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he said: 'My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous'?
He only asked Allah, Exalted and Mighty, to grant him a boy from among the righteous. And He said in the Surah As-Saffat: 'So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.'
Meaning Ismail from Hajer. So He said: 'So We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Then He said: 'And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet, from among the righteous. And We blessed him and Ishaq.'

He means by it Ismail before the glad tidings of Ishaq. So whoever claims that Ishaq is older than Ismail and that the one to be sacrificed was Ishaq, has lied regarding what Allah, Exalted and Mighty, revealed in the Quran about their stories.
ai.seo_question: Who was the son sacrificed by Prophet Ibrahim, Ismail or Ishaq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the chronological precedence of Ismail over Ishaq by five years, linking the glad tidings in Surah As-Saffat to Ismail’s birth from Hajar before the promise of Ishaq. He argues that the phrase 'and blessed him and with Ishaq' in the Quran refers back to Ismail, thereby refuting the view that Ishaq was the primary sacrifice and affirming the event occurred at Mina during the Hajj season. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly consensus on the identity of the sacrificed son, grounding the narrative in both Quranic exegesis and the specific timeline of Ibrahim’s life.

en.basel-kadem: 33. We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Salama bin Khattab, from Hussain bin Rashid bin Yahya, from Ali bin Isma’eel, from Amru bin Abi’l-Miqdam, that he said: I heard Abu’l-Hasan or Abu Ja’far, peace be upon them both, say with regards to this verse: «nor do they disobey you with regards to a good thing» [60:12].

He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said to Fatima, peace be upon her: When I will die, do not slap any face for my sake, nor unstring any hair for my sake, nor call with woe, nor perform any mourning for my sake.
He then said: This is the good thing about which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said in His Book: «nor do they disobey you with regards to a good thing». [60:12]
